claims.claim_ar: أداة القصر «مِمَّا» تقيد الإنفاق بمصدر محدّد: «مِمَّا رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ» — أي الإنفاق يكون من ما رزقهم الله لا من موارد أخرى.
claims.claim_en: The restrictive particle/relative 'مِمَّا' confines the spending to a specific source: 'from what Allah has provided them' — i.e., spending is restricted to provisions given by God, not other means.
claims.needs_review_reason: The reading in the provided source chunk is 'بِما أَنْفَقُوا' (similar but not identical); classification of the particle here as 'hasr_qasr' (restrictive qualification) is plausible but should be checked against classical terminology in the cited tafsir/بلاغة authors.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار لفظ الجلالة «اللَّه» في المعنى لضبط المبتدأ/الفاعل والتوكيد: «رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ ... وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ عَلِيمًا».
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the Divine Name 'Allah' functions as emphatic repetition to fix the agent and to emphasize God's knowledge: 'Allah provided them ... and Allah was, concerning them, Knowing.'

claims.claim_ar: استعمال «لَوْ» في صيغة تخيلية/استنكارية للتوبيخ والتقريع: «وَمَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ آمَنُوا ...» يُعرض كاستنكار لما تفي به نفوسهم.
claims.claim_en: The conditional particle 'لَوْ' is used in a counterfactual/rhetorical way to express reproach or incredulity: 'What [harm] would it be to them if they had believed ...' — framed as a reproachful hypothetical.
claims.needs_review_reason: Classification as a rhetorical reproach (vs. simple counterfactual) should be verified against classical rhetorical labels (e.g., whether jurjani/sakkaki call this usage a specific device).
